model.expr: ((group by (instance_id) (count_over_time(fluxtube_runs[2h])) and group by (instance_id) (count_over_time(fluxtube_runs[1d] offset 6d))) unless group by (instance_id) (count_over_time(fluxtube_backup_runs_total{outcome="success"}[7d]))) or (absent_over_time(fluxtube_backup_runs_total{outcome="success"}[7d]) unless on () count(count_over_time(fluxtube_runs[2h])))

annotations.summary: No successful FluxTube backup in the last 7 days.
annotations.description: No successful backup in the last 7 days. The query returns a row only when a backup is missing, so an empty result (NoData) means healthy and `noDataState` is `OK`; do not flip it to `Alerting`, which would fire whenever backups are fine. Two branches: (1) an instance whose sync Worker is reporting runs now and was already reporting them 6 to 7 days ago (so a new instance is not flagged in its first week), but which has no successful backup in 7 days, labelled with its `instance_id`; (2) no successful backup anywhere and no sync runs either, which is a full metric-shipping outage or a stopped stack, with no `instance_id` label. A failing backup still counts as missing: only `outcome="success"` clears it. Check the /dashboard/backup page for the last-attempted timestamp, tail the dashboard Worker's logs (`wrangler tail --name fluxtube-<instance_id>-dashboard`), and verify the BACKUPS R2 binding (`wrangler r2 object list fluxtube-<instance_id>-backups`).
